newsitem.title: USA: USDA FCOJ estimate seen at 205 mln-210 mln boxes.
newsitem.headline: USDA FCOJ estimate seen at 205 mln-210 mln boxes.

text.p: Analysts expect the U.S. Department of Agriculture to revise its estimate of the Florida orange crop to 205 million to 210 million 90-lb boxes for the current season, in its widely-anticipated report released Wednesday.
Previously, the USDA put the 1996/97 crop at a record 220-million boxes. Yields were seen at 1.50 gallons per box compared with the earlier estimate of 1.53 gallons per box.
The report, which includes the first official estimate of the crop since the Jan 19 freeze, is not expected to nudge frozen concentrated orange juice (FCOJ) futures out of their recent trading range.
"It's already in the market," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said.
She said an estimate below 200 million boxes could lift prices, "but even then they may not move too dramatically. We had a decent size carryover, demand is softer and imports greater."
Bernard Savaiko, an analyst with PaineWebber, agreed.
"We are not bringing prices down at the retail level to stimulate demand, the dollar is still relatively resiliant and could be hurting exports to European countries and maybe even Japan," he said.
Savaiko said market activity since the freeze relects a 5 percent loss, or a crop of about 209 million boxes. He put yields at 1.51 gallons per box.
But Allendale analyst Jim Cordier said the forecast could fuel futures prices higher, and pegged the estimate at 206 million boxes.
"If prices were over a dollor (the losses) would already be factored in, but prices are a bit on the low side," Cordier said.
He said retailers should lower orange juice prices and stimulate demand in the near term. From a technical standpoint, the lows have been made, he added.
